title: Recognition of coherent weighted homotopy limit cones
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, coherent cones and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent realization and simplicial categories of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $Y$ be a small simplicial set, $A=\mathfrak C[Y]$, and $B=\mathfrak C[\Delta^0\star Y]$, with new first vertex $b$. Define $W_Y:A\to\mathrm{sSet}$ by $W_Y(a)=B(b,a)$ and postcomposition. Let $\mathcal D$ be a simplicial category with Kan mapping simplicial sets, let $F:A\to\mathcal D$ be an enriched functor, let $L\in\mathcal D$, and let $\lambda:W_Y\to\mathcal D(L,F(-))$ be an enriched natural transformation. Here $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(P,Q)_n$ consists of enriched natural maps $P\times\Delta^n\to Q$. Suppose, for every $Z\in\mathcal D$, postcomposition with $\lambda$ gives a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\mathcal D(Z,L)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W_Y,\mathcal D(Z,F(-))).$$
Then the coherent cone determined by $\lambda$, whose enriched collage is the functor $B\to\mathcal D$ restricting to $F$ and sending $b$ to $L$, is a limit cone on $Y\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal D$. Here a join cone $\Delta^0\star Y\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal D$ is called a limit cone when its image under the fixed-boundary, fixed-vertex comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] is a limiting cone in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The coherent nerve and the boundary diagram here use the subset-poset realization/nerve adjunction of [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure].

source.place: Riehl–Verity, Recognizing quasi-categorical limits and colimits in homotopy coherent nerves, Definition 5.2.8 (p. 34), Definition 4.1.8 (p. 22) and Theorem 6.1.4 with proof (pp. 43–49). Read the authors’ online PDF; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-join-boundary-cubical-extension], $B$ is the enriched collage of $W_Y$. Thus $\lambda$ specifies a functor $\Lambda:B\to\mathcal D$: it equals $F$ on $A$, takes $b$ to $L$, and acts on $B(b,a)$ by $\lambda_a$. The functor equations on the mixed compositions are precisely the enriched naturality equations for $\lambda$. The subset-poset formulas in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] give the adjunction directly: a functor $\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathcal D$ is a compatible family of functors on all simplices of $K$, hence a simplicial map $K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal D$. Consequently $\Lambda$ determines the actual join cone $\ell$ on the transposed boundary diagram $d:Y\to C=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal D$. This construction commutes with restriction of any parameter simplex. By [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory], $C$ is a quasicategory, since every mapping set of $\mathcal D$ is Kan.

The mapping simplicial sets $T_Z=\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W_Y,G_Z)$, where $G_Z=\mathcal D(Z,F(-))$, are Kan. Indeed [lem-coef-join-cone-weight-cofibrancy] applies to the small simplicial set $Y$, without any local Kan condition on $A=\mathfrak C[Y]$, and makes precisely the outgoing weight $W_Y$ projectively cofibrant. The Kan model structure is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Consequently [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] applies to its enriched diagrams over the small simplicial category $A$. The diagram $G_Z$ is projectively fibrant because each $\mathcal D(Z,F(a))$ is Kan. Apply the simplicial model axiom in this projective model structure to the cofibration $\varnothing\to W_Y$ and fibration $G_Z\to1$. Its induced mapping map is $T_Z\to1$, since maps from the initial diagram or to the terminal diagram are unique. It is a Kan fibration, proving the assertion. The mapping set has the degree-$n$ enriched natural maps $W_Y\times\Delta^n\to G_Z$ specified in the item, since tensors and mapping ends are the stated objectwise ones.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.9 and Proposition 4.1.5: cofibrancy of the coherent weight and fibrancy of its weighted ends; expressed through existing projective-model interfaces.

proof.text: We show directly that $\ell$ is terminal in the join slice $C_{/d}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For an arbitrary $n\ge1$, a boundary $\partial\Delta^n\to C_{/d}$ with last vertex $\ell$ is a map $\partial\Delta^n\star Y\to C$ with boundary $d$ and last cone $\ell$. Indeed maps from any simplicial set into this slice are compatible families of its defining join simplices; taking the union over boundary faces gives precisely that join map. By Step 1 it is equivalent to an enriched functor $H:\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n\star Y]\to\mathcal D$ with last cone $\Lambda$. Apply [lem-coef-join-boundary-cubical-extension]. With $Z=H(0)$, the two targets of its cubical problem are $M=\mathcal D(Z,L)$ and $T=T_Z$, and its map $u:M\to T$ is exactly composition with the given $\lambda$. Both targets are Kan by the local Kan hypothesis and Step 2, and $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by the assumed weak homotopy equivalence for every object $Z$ of $\mathcal D$, applied at $Z=H(0)$. The only missing extension data are $a:Q\to M$ and $c:Q\times\Delta^1\to T$, with precisely the three boundary equations in that lemma.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.8, (6.1.10), and the cubical presentation at the end of printed p. 45; fix the last vertex cone before solving the extension.

proof.text: Factor this particular weak equivalence by paths. Define $E=M\times_{T,u,\mathrm{ev}_1}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,T)$ and $e:E\to T$ by $e(m,\gamma)=\gamma(0)$. The Cartesian simplicial-model axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $T\to1$, makes the two-endpoint map a Kan fibration. Thus $E\to T\times M$ is a Kan fibration; composing with $T\times M\to T$, which is a pullback of $M\to1$, makes $e$ a Kan fibration. These pullback and composition closures are model-category consequences recorded by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Endpoint evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_1:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,T)\to T$ is a trivial fibration by the same simplicial-model axiom, since $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is the one-dimensional horn inclusion and hence a trivial cofibration. Its pullback $q:E\to M$ is a trivial fibration. The constant-path section $s:M\to E$ satisfies $qs=1_M$, so $s$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Since $es=u$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three also makes $e$ a weak equivalence. Therefore $e$ is a trivial fibration. This argument does not require $u$ itself to be a Kan fibration.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.11 and the terminal-base specialization of Lemma 6.1.13: explicit mapping-path factorization replaces the comma-object notation.

proof.text: Transpose the known $\beta|_{\partial Q\times\Delta^1}$ and pair it with $\alpha$ to obtain a map $\partial Q\to E$. The equality $\beta|_{\partial Q\times\{1\}}=u\alpha$ is exactly the defining pullback equation of $E$. The bottom face $\beta|_{Q\times\{0\}}$ gives a map $Q\to T$, agreeing after $e$ with this boundary map. Since $\partial Q\hookrightarrow Q$ is degreewise injective, the trivial fibration $e$ lifts this square. For completeness the model-structure node says every monomorphism is built from boundary inclusions, and trivial fibrations lift all such inclusions, so the lift exists for this cube boundary as well. Write the lift as $(a,c)$ under the exponential adjunction. Its boundary and projection equations give $a|_{\partial Q}=\alpha$, $c|_V=\beta$, $c|_{Q\times\{1\}}=ua$. The cubical-extension lemma therefore produces an extension $\overline H:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star Y]\to\mathcal D$ of the original $H$. Transposing back gives an extension of the chosen boundary in $C_{/d}$. The case $n=1$ is included: $Q=\Delta^0$, $\partial Q=\varnothing$, so this is the dimension-zero lifting property of a trivial fibration, not an omitted nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.11 and Corollary 6.1.16, with the relative cube boundary and n=1 written explicitly.

proof.text: Put $Q=C_{/d}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], $Q$ is a quasicategory, so $Q\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration. Every right-pinched mapping space of $\Delta^0$ is $\Delta^0$. Therefore the final clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary], applied over $\Delta^0$, says that a vertex $t$ of $Q$ is terminal exactly when every boundary $\partial\Delta^m\to Q$ with $m\ge1$ and last vertex $t$ extends to $\Delta^m$. Step 5 proves precisely this property for $t=\ell$. Thus $\ell$ is terminal in the join slice. The initial clause of the same node gives the corresponding criterion with first vertex $t$; we will use that clause to handle the opposite convention without identifying left-pinched and right-pinched mapping spaces.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.4 proof on printed p. 49 and Example 3.2.6: terminal boundary test, followed by the existing join-slice/comma comparison in its dual form.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-opposite-join-comma-comparison] to the small diagram $d:Y\to C$ obtained in Step 1. It supplies the quasicategory $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, the diagram $a=d^{\mathrm{op}}$ and simplicial isomorphisms $R:Q^{\mathrm{op}}\cong J_a$ and $S:(\Delta_Y\downarrow d)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong P_a$, where $Q=C_{/d}$. In particular these are isomorphisms on all boundary simplices, with first and last vertices exchanged by reversal, not just bijections on objects. The comparison $r_a:J_a\to P_a$ is the specified fat-join comparison of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Both $J_a$ and $P_a$ are quasicategories by that node.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.4 proof on printed p. 49 and Example 3.2.6: terminal boundary test, followed by the existing join-slice/comma comparison in its dual form.

proof.text: A boundary in $J_a\cong Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ with first vertex $R_0(\ell)$ reverses to a boundary in $Q$ with last vertex $\ell$. Step 5 supplies its extension. The initial boundary criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary], applied over $\Delta^0$, makes $R_0(\ell)$ initial in $J_a$. By [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], $r_{a,0}(R_0(\ell))$ is initial in $P_a$. The same criterion gives every boundary extension with that first vertex in $P_a$. Through the simplicial isomorphism $S$ of [lem-coef-opposite-join-comma-comparison], these are exactly the boundary extensions in $(\Delta_Y\downarrow d)$ with last vertex $v=S_0^{-1}(r_{a,0}(R_0(\ell)))$. This comma category is a quasicategory: its opposite is isomorphic to $P_a$, and reversing an inner horn $\Lambda_i^m$ gives the inner horn $\Lambda_{m-i}^m$. The final boundary criterion therefore makes $v$ terminal, hence limiting by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 6.1.4 proof on printed p. 49 and Example 3.2.6: terminal boundary test, followed by the existing join-slice/comma comparison in its dual form.

proof.text: The last clause of [lem-coef-opposite-join-comma-comparison] identifies the vertex $v$ of Step 8 with $\ell$ precomposed with the actual collapse $T_Y\to\Delta^0\star Y$ of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. It fixes the entire boundary and the cone vertex. Thus the cone proved limiting in Step 8 is precisely the fixed-boundary, fixed-vertex comparison image specified in the statement, which proves the conclusion.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.4 proof on printed p. 49 and Example 3.2.6: terminal boundary test, followed by the existing join-slice/comma comparison in its dual form.

proof_origin.place: Retained join-boundary proof following Riehl–Verity §§5.2–5.3 and 6.1, checked against the published author-hosted PDF; mapping-path factorization expanded directly, and the fixed-boundary comma comparison expanded using existing DAG nodes. Archival copy WANTED.
